subject: Energy
title: The Renewable Rise
description: Learn The Renewable Rise in one minute.

hook.text: Solar and wind were expensive curiosities in the 1990s—today they are the cheapest new electricity sources on Earth.

buildup.text: Germany's feed-in tariff (2000) created early demand—paying homeowners premium rates for solar, jumpstarting the market.

discovery.text: China scaled manufacturing massively after 2010—solar panel costs fell 90% in a decade due to incredible volume.

twist.text: Renewables now attract more investment than fossil fuels—over $500 billion annually, as economics shift decisively.

climax.text: In 2023, renewables generated over 30% of global electricity for the first time—the transition is accelerating.

punchline.text: Once too expensive—now too cheap to ignore. Renewables won.

quiz.question: What drove the massive drop in solar panel costs after 2010?
